A1.justification: Both PDFs are 20-page versions of What Matters in Data for DPO?, including Appendices A–B. Their text, equations, figures and tables are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 5 and Tables 1–4 report original DPO experiments examining response quality, online DPO versus continual SFT, preference gaps and on-policy data mixtures.

after.justification: Section 5 and Tables 1–4 retain the original DPO training and evaluation results, including controlled response-quality and on-policy experiments.

M1.justification: The DPO objective, fixed-chosen online DPO procedure and Algorithm 1's data-generation and mixing steps are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both use Open Assistant 2 and UltraFeedback and evaluate on AlpacaEval-2, MMLU, IFEval, TruthfulQA and GSM8K. The evaluated scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain the same SFT baseline and continual-SFT/Online-DPO comparisons. Appendix B.1 also retains the same reward-model versus LLM-as-a-judge selection comparison.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 and Appendix B retain the same 8B model, filtered prompt counts, training budgets, sampling procedures, metrics and benchmark testing settings.

E4.justification: The controlled chosen/rejected-quality comparisons, preference-gap counterfactuals, on-policy mixture analysis and Appendix B.1 evaluator-selection analysis are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both state that benchmark results average three independent runs with different random seeds in Section 5.1. Statistical and uncertainty reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: The numerical results in Tables 1–5 and associated qualitative findings match. For example, UltraFeedback Best/Worst retains 36.5 LC-AE2 and 80.4 GSM8K in Table 1.

T1.justification: Theorems 4.1, 4.3 and 4.5, Propositions 4.2 and 4.4, their assumptions and the Appendix A proofs are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about chosen-response quality, the role of contrastiveness and the connection between simplified online DPO and SFT.

C2.justification: Interpretations of response quality, preference gaps and on-policy mixing are unchanged. Appendix B.1 retains the same reward-model calibration caveats and justification.

D1.justification: Appendix B retains the same dataset construction, hyperparameters, evaluation instructions, hardware and timing disclosures. No technical or code/data-access information is added or removed.

R1.justification: Section 3 and the bibliography contain the same cited works and research positioning, including the discussions of data quality and on-policy DPO.

P1.justification: Page 1 changes the corresponding author from Chonghuan Wang to Yu Pan, moving the asterisk and replacing the contact email. The arXiv version/date stamp also changes; the prose and section structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1, Tables 1–7 and Algorithm 1 retain their graphics, structure, captions and placement. Visual inspection establishes no figure, table or page-layout revision.

improvement.justification: v2 updates correspondence details and the version/date stamp while retaining the same theory, experiments, results, explanations and appendix material. These administrative edits do not meaningfully alter the paper's overall quality.
